text:
julia.ops: Hi, after upgrading our app to python-sdk 1.32.0 we started seeing a spike of 401s and a billing surge. Looks like retries fire even on 401 and we get charged twice for the same request. Anyone seen this?
alex.support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the SDK version + a minimal repro? also which auth method (API key / oauth)? :thinking_face: 
julia.ops: API key. repro is simple: single POST to /v1/generate, we get a 401 first, client retries and the second attempt succeeds but we got billed twice in our invoice. SDK version: 1.32.0. requests in stack:
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = c.generate(model='rwx-13b', prompt='hi')
print(resp.status_code)
```
ryan.eng: thanks — tagging eng. quick note: we changed how transient auth errors surface in 1.31->1.32, and there was also a rename of the timeout param (timeout_ms -> timeout_seconds) that caused some callers to accidentally pass an unexpected kwarg which the client ignored, falling back to a default retry policy. could be related.
maya.devx: alex can you ask for the full client logs including X-Request-Id and the SDK debug logs? running with REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 will print retry decisions.
alex.support: julia, can you enable REDWOOD_DEBUG and paste the small snippet of logs around the 401? also share request ids from billing spike if possible.
julia.ops: logs attached (excerpt):
```
DEBUG redwood.client Retrying request id=rid_abc123 reason=401
INFO redwood.client Request succeeded id=rid_abc123 attempt=2 elapsed_ms=120
```
we also saw header: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>` on both attempts. invoice shows two 0.002 tokens entries at the same minute.
sara.billing: I've started a billing ticket to investigate duplicate line items; please include the request ids. we can refund if clearly duplicate but need to confirm retries are idempotent.
ryan.eng: this looks like the client treated 401 as retryable. That's a bug — 4xx non-idempotent auth failures should not trigger automatic retries. root cause: retry config was refactored and a default retry map was tightened but the mapping of status codes got inverted for auth in a hotfix branch that landed in 1.32.0.
ryan.eng: short-term mitigation: pin to 1.30.2 which has the previous retry behavior. long-term we'll cut 1.32.1 to restore correct mapping and add unit coverage.
alex.support: workaround for customers who can't pin right away: set env var REDWOOD_RETRY_STRICT=1 to disable retry-on-4xx (internal toggled flag we can set per-tenant) — julia, we can flip it for your org while we publish the patch.
julia.ops: can you flip it? we have prod traffic. also what's the easiest way to pin in our pip/poetry?
maya.devx: in pip: `pip install 'redwood-sdk==1.30.2'` or add to requirements.txt `redwood-sdk==1.30.2`. for poetry: `poetry add redwood-sdk@1.30.2` (or put it in pyproject).
ryan.eng: note: some customers depended on the timeout_ms alias which was removed in 1.32; if you relied on that you need to rename to `timeout_seconds` in your client config. if you pass an unknown kwarg the client previously ignored it silently; new versions are stricter so please check your config.
alex.support: I've escalated this to on-call eng and billing. @sara.billing is handling refunds. @ryan.eng will publish a 1.32.1 patch and a changelog note.
sara.billing: refund queued for the clearly duplicate charges tied to rid_abc123 and related ids — I'll follow up in the billing ticket.
julia.ops: thanks everyone. please confirm when you flip REDWOOD_RETRY_STRICT for our org (org-id: org_789).
ryan.eng: done — flag flipped for org_789. we expect no more retry-on-401. shipping 1.32.1 today; I'll post the release thread when it's live.
alex.support: follow-up: when 1.32.1 is published, we recommend customers either pin to 1.30.2 or upgrade directly to 1.32.1. we'll also publish a migration note about the timeout_ms -> timeout_seconds rename and the new behavior. :white_check_mark:
julia.ops: confirmed errors stopped after flag flip. thanks for the fast turnaround.
